statements.impact_statement: The affected image-size parser is reachable only through web-ext while maintainers lint or package committed companion-extension files. Blanc does not pass network, user, or release-time input to this parser.

The affected image-size parser is reachable only through web-ext while maintainers lint or package committed companion-extension files. Blanc does not pass network, user, or release-time input to this parser.

The affected adm-zip extraction is a development-only web-ext path operating on committed companion-extension sources and a maintainer-selected local output directory. It is absent from Blanc release payloads and receives no untrusted archive or destination path.

Reviewed by Claude on 2026-10-06 and approved by the owner: sprintf-js 1.1.3 occurs only under development-only electron-builder (via @electron/get 3.1.0, its optional global-agent 3.0.0, and roarr 2.15.4). @electron/get loads global-agent only when ELECTRON_GET_USE_PROXY is set, which no Blanc script, workflow, or configuration does, and every global-agent log call passes a constant format string, so no adversary controls the precision specifier the advisory requires. Absent from the desktop runtime graph, release payloads, the website, and the tab-import Worker and companions. Evidence and re-review conditions: docs/security-reviews/2026-10-06-sprintf-js.md.

picomatch is reached only by build tooling: in the desktop app through development dependencies (electron-builder, @electron/rebuild, node-gyp), never packaged; on the website through Astro's static build (output: 'static', no server adapter or functions). Every glob it evaluates comes from committed configuration and source, never from network, user or release-time input. No patched picomatch exists yet (<= 4.0.7 affected).

The affected minimatch copies are reached only by development tooling (electron-builder's app-builder-lib, @electron/universal, @electron/asar and their build helpers), which match globs from committed build configuration. None is packaged, and no network, user or release-time input reaches them. Listed because the dependency policy counts every advisory of a package flagged high (here through GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf).

Astro runs only at build time: the website is output: 'static' with no server adapter or functions, and every dynamic tag name it renders comes from committed source. A visitor cannot supply the tag names the advisory requires. Fixed in astro 7.4.5; the site update is tracked separately.

The vulnerable image endpoint exists only when a site is served by the @astrojs/node adapter. Blanc's website is output: 'static', has no adapter (no @astrojs/node in site/package-lock.json) and serves prebuilt files from Cloudflare Pages, so no request reaches Astro's image endpoint. Fixed in astro 7.4.7; the site update is tracked separately.
